citations.B1: Check-then-increment is not atomic across threads, so concurrent requests past the limit are both allowed
citations.B2: concurrent requests past the limit are both allowed and increments are lost
citations.B3: guard the read-modify-write with a lock or use an atomic increment
citations.B4: No time window: counts never reset, so a user is blocked forever after 100 requests
citations.B5: Unbounded memory: every user_id ever seen stays in the dict; evict entries on window expiry
citations.B6: `counts` is per-process, so N workers each enforce their own limit and the real limit is N×100
citations.B7: `None` becomes a shared bucket, and unhashable ids raise `TypeError`; validate and normalise user_id
